title: Factors, Multiples, Primes, HCF and LCM
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Mathematics 0862 · Stage 8 · Number
summary: Find factors and multiples, test for primes, write numbers as products of prime factors, and use them to find the HCF and LCM in problems.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Understand factors, multiples and prime factors; write a number as a product of its prime factors; find the highest common factor (HCF) and the lowest common multiple (LCM) of numbers, and use them to solve problems (8Ni.03)

blocks.text: Every whole number bigger than 1 is built from prime numbers, in the same way that every word is built from letters. On this page you will learn how to break a number into its **prime factors**, and how to use them to find the **highest common factor (HCF)** and **lowest common multiple (LCM)** quickly — even for big numbers. These skills appear on both papers and are used again in fractions, ratio and algebra.
Key words

items: factor
عامل / قاسم — a whole number that divides exactly into another: 6 is a factor of 24
multiple
مضاعف — the result of multiplying by a whole number: 24 is a multiple of 6
prime number
عدد أولي — has exactly two factors, 1 and itself: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …
composite number
عدد غير أولي (مؤلف) — has more than two factors: 4, 6, 8, 9, …
prime factor
عامل أولي — a factor that is also prime: the prime factors of 12 are 2 and 3
product of prime factors
تحليل العدد إلى عوامله الأولية — 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 = 2^{2} × 3
index form
صورة الأسس — writing repeated factors with powers: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2^{3}
highest common factor (HCF)
القاسم المشترك الأكبر (ق.م.أ) — the biggest number that is a factor of both numbers
lowest common multiple (LCM)
المضاعف المشترك الأصغر (م.م.أ) — the smallest number that is a multiple of both numbers

blocks.text: 1. Factors and multiples

**Find factors in pairs.** Start at 1 and work upwards: 1 × 36, 2 × 36… ask "does 2 divide 36? does 3?" Each time you find one factor, you also get its partner. Stop when the numbers meet in the middle. For 36 the pairs are joined like a rainbow:

blocks.text: **Multiples** go on for ever: the multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, … If a is a factor of b, then b is a multiple of a. So "6 is a factor of 42" and "42 is a multiple of 6" say the same thing.

rows: the sum of the digits is a multiple of 3
the last two digits make a multiple of 4
it is divisible by 2 and by 3
the last three digits make a multiple of 8
the sum of the digits is a multiple of 9

blocks.text: 2. Prime numbers
A **prime number** has **exactly two** factors: 1 and itself. The primes less than 50 are:

items: **1 is not prime** — it has only one factor.
**2 is the only even prime.** Every other even number has 2 as a factor, so it has more than two factors.

**To test whether a number is prime**, try dividing it by the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, … You only need to try primes up to the square root of the number. For 97: √97 is just under 10, so try 2, 3, 5 and 7. None divides 97, so **97 is prime**. For 91: 91 ÷ 7 = 13, so **91 is not prime** (91 = 7 × 13).

blocks.text: 3. Writing a number as a product of prime factors
Every whole number greater than 1 can be written as a product of primes in **exactly one way** (apart from the order). There are two methods.
**Method 1: factor tree.** Split the number into any factor pair, then keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime. Ring the primes as you go.

blocks.text: **Method 2: repeated division (the ladder).** Divide by the smallest prime that goes in exactly, again and again, until you reach 1. Example: 252.

So 252 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 = **2^{2} × 3^{2} × 7**. Always write the primes in order from smallest to largest, and use index form when a question asks for it. Check by multiplying back: 4 × 9 × 7 = 36 × 7 = 252 ✓.
**Using prime factors.** Once you know 360 = 2^{3} × 3^{2} × 5, you can answer questions without dividing:

items: Is 360 divisible by 7? 7 is not one of its prime factors. **No.**
Is 360 divisible by 27? 27 = 3^{3}, but 360 only has 3^{2}. **No.**
**Square numbers** have every prime factor to an even power: 144 = 2^{4} × 3^{2}. 360 = 2^{3} × 3^{2} × 5 is not square, because 2^{3} and 5 have odd powers.

blocks.text: 4. Highest common factor (HCF)
**Listing method (small numbers).** HCF of 18 and 24: factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, **6**, 9, 18; factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, **6**, 8, 12, 24. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, so the HCF is **6**.
**Prime factor method (any numbers).** Write both numbers as products of primes. The HCF is the product of the primes they **share**, using the **smaller** power of each shared prime.
84 = 2^{2} × 3 × 7 and 90 = 2 × 3^{2} × 5. Shared primes: 2 (smaller power 2^{1}) and 3 (smaller power 3^{1}). HCF = 2 × 3 = **6**.
5. Lowest common multiple (LCM)
**Listing method.** LCM of 6 and 8: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, **24**, 30, …; multiples of 8 are 8, 16, **24**, 32, … The first one in both lists is **24**.

**Prime factor method.** The LCM uses **every** prime that appears in either number, with the **larger** power of each. For 84 = 2^{2} × 3 × 7 and 90 = 2 × 3^{2} × 5: LCM = 2^{2} × 3^{2} × 5 × 7 = 4 × 9 × 35 = **1260**.
6. The Venn diagram method (HCF and LCM together)
Put the prime factors of each number in a circle. Shared primes go in the overlap — **once only**. Then:

items: **HCF = multiply the numbers in the overlap.**
**LCM = multiply every number in the diagram.**

blocks.text: **A useful generalisation:** for two numbers, HCF × LCM = the product of the numbers. Check: 6 × 1260 = 7560 and 84 × 90 = 7560 ✓. This is because every prime factor of the two numbers is used exactly once in HCF × LCM.

blocks.title: ق.م.أ و م.م.أ بسهولة
items: حلّل كل عدد لعوامله الأولية (شجرة العوامل أو القسمة المتكررة).
ق.م.أ (HCF): خد العوامل المشتركة بس — بالأس الأصغر. في شكل فن = اللي في النص.
م.م.أ (LCM): خد كل العوامل — بالأس الأكبر. في شكل فن = اضرب كل الأرقام اللي في الشكل.
الرقم 1 مش عدد أولي، و 2 هو العدد الأولي الزوجي الوحيد.

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Write 360 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form. [2 marks]

items: Order the primes: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5.
Check: 8 × 9 × 5 = 72 × 5 = 360 ✓. (Mark scheme style: 1 mark for a correct list of prime factors, e.g. 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5; 1 mark for the index form.)

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** leaving a non-prime in the answer, such as 2^{3} × 9 × 5, or writing it as a sum (2 + 2 + …).
**Worked example 2** — Find (a) the HCF and (b) the LCM of 48 and 180. [3 marks]

items: (a) Shared primes with the smaller powers: 2^{2} and 3. HCF = 4 × 3 = **12**.
(b) Every prime with the larger power: 2^{4}, 3^{2} and 5. LCM = 16 × 9 × 5 = 144 × 5 = **720**.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** swapping the rules — using the larger powers for the HCF. The HCF can never be bigger than the smaller number (48).
**Worked example 3** — Two buses leave the bus station at 7:00. Bus A leaves every 12 minutes and bus B every 18 minutes. At what time do they next leave together? [2 marks]

items: "Together again" → LCM of 12 and 18.
Multiples of 12: 12, 24, **36**, … Multiples of 18: 18, **36**, … LCM = 36.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** giving 36 as the answer — the question asks for a time.

**Worked example 4** — Salma has a ribbon 72 cm long and another ribbon 120 cm long. She cuts both ribbons into pieces that are all the same length, with nothing left over. The pieces must be as long as possible. (a) How long is each piece? (b) How many pieces does she get altogether? [3 marks]

items: "Largest equal pieces" → HCF of 72 and 120.
(b) 72 ÷ 24 = 3 pieces and 120 ÷ 24 = 5 pieces, so **8 pieces** altogether.

blocks.text: **Worked example 5** — Is 221 a prime number? Show how you decide. [2 marks]

items: 221 is odd; 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 (not divisible by 3); it does not end in 0 or 5; 221 ÷ 7 = 31.57…; 221 ÷ 11 = 20.09…
221 ÷ 13 = 17 exactly.
So 221 = 13 × 17 and **221 is not prime**.

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** saying 221 is prime because it is not divisible by 2, 3 or 5. You must test every prime up to the square root.
**Worked example 6** — N = 2^{3} × 3 × 5^{2}. (a) Is N a multiple of 12? (b) Is N a multiple of 9? (c) Find the smallest whole number you can multiply N by to make a square number. [3 marks]

items: (a) 12 = 2^{2} × 3. N contains 2^{3} (which includes 2^{2}) and 3, so **yes**.
(b) 9 = 3^{2}, but N only contains 3^{1}. So **no**.
(c) A square number has even powers. 2^{3} needs one more 2; 3^{1} needs one more 3; 5^{2} is already even. Multiply by 2 × 3 = **6**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Calling 1 a prime number, or forgetting that 2 is prime.
Thinking every odd number is prime: 9, 15, 21, 27, 51, 57, 91 are all composite.
Leaving composite numbers in a factor tree answer (e.g. 2 × 4 × 9).
Mixing up HCF and LCM. The HCF is never bigger than the smaller number; the LCM is never smaller than the bigger number.
Thinking the LCM is always the product of the two numbers. That only works when the HCF is 1: LCM(4, 6) = 12, not 24.
In a Venn diagram, putting a shared prime in both circles and the overlap — each shared prime goes in the overlap only.
Answering a time problem with just the number of minutes.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Write 252 as a product of its prime factors" — give a product (×), in index form if asked. Show the tree or ladder: it can earn a part mark.
"Find the HCF/LCM of …" — often [1] or [2]. With large numbers, use prime factors or a Venn diagram.
Numbers given already in prime-factor form, e.g. "A = 2^{2} × 3 × 7. Find the HCF of A and B" — do not multiply out first; work with the primes.
Word problems with buses, lights, tiles, packets or groups — decide HCF or LCM from the table above, and answer in the units the question uses.
"Ring the prime numbers" or "Explain why 119 is not prime" — give a factor pair as evidence (119 = 7 × 17).
Statements to test: "The LCM of two numbers is always their product." One counter-example proves it false.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Factors, primes, HCF and LCM practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, no calculator. Use factor trees or the ladder on paper, then type your answers. Every question has a full solution.

questions.q: Which of these numbers is prime?
questions.e: 51 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19, 87 = 3 × 29 (each has digit sum divisible by 3). 59 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 7 (√59 < 8), so 59 is prime.
Factor pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. Factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36 — that is 9 factors (6 is counted once).

questions.q: Which shows 90 written as a product of its prime factors?
questions.e: 90 = 2 × 45 = 2 × 3 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2 × 3^{2} × 5. The other answers contain numbers that are not prime (9, 10, 45, 15).

questions.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 60.
questions.e: 24 = 2^{3} × 3 and 60 = 2^{2} × 3 × 5. Shared primes with smaller powers: 2^{2} × 3 = 12. (Check: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 60 ÷ 12 = 5, and 2 and 5 share no factor.)

questions.q: Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 8 and 14.
questions.e: Multiples of 14: 14, 28, 42, 56, … The first one that is a multiple of 8 is 56. Or: 8 = 2^{3}, 14 = 2 × 7, LCM = 2^{3} × 7 = 56.

questions.q: (a) Find the HCF of P and Q.
questions.e: Shared primes with the smaller power: 2^{1}, 3^{1}, 7^{1}. HCF = 2 × 3 × 7 = 42. (P = 84, Q = 126.)

questions.q: (b) Find the LCM of P and Q.
questions.e: Every prime with the larger power: 2^{2} × 3^{2} × 7 = 4 × 9 × 7 = 252. Check: HCF × LCM = 42 × 252 = 10 584 = 84 × 126 ✓.

questions.q: Two lights flash at the same moment. One flashes every 18 seconds and the other every 24 seconds. After how many seconds do they next flash together?
A floor is 150 cm by 210 cm. It is covered exactly with identical square tiles, with no cutting. What is the side length of the largest tile that can be used?
questions.e: The tile side must divide both 150 and 210 exactly, and be as large as possible → HCF. 150 = 2 × 3 × 5^{2}, 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7. HCF = 2 × 3 × 5 = 30 cm. (5 tiles by 7 tiles.)

questions.q: Ali says, "The LCM of two numbers is always the two numbers multiplied together." Which pair of numbers shows that Ali is wrong?
questions.e: 4 × 6 = 24, but the LCM of 4 and 6 is 12 (12 is a multiple of both). For 3 and 5, 2 and 7, and 5 and 9 the LCM does equal the product, because those pairs have HCF 1.

questions.q: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 72. One of the numbers is 18. Find the other number.
questions.e: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers, so 6 × 72 = 432 = 18 × other. Other = 432 ÷ 18 = 24. Check: HCF(18, 24) = 6 and LCM(18, 24) = 72 ✓.

questions.q: Explain how you know that 119 is not a prime number.
questions.ms: 1 mark: shows a factor other than 1 and 119, e.g. 119 = 7 × 17 or 119 ÷ 7 = 17. Do not accept "it is odd" or "it ends in 9" — these are not reasons.
questions.e: Test primes up to √119 (about 10.9): 2 no, 3 no (1 + 1 + 9 = 11), 5 no, 7: 119 ÷ 7 = 17 exactly. So 119 = 7 × 17. It has factors other than 1 and itself, so it is not prime.

questions.q: 40 = 2^{3} × 5. What is the smallest whole number you can multiply 40 by to make a square number?
questions.e: A square number has every prime to an even power. 2^{3} needs one more 2 and 5^{1} needs one more 5, so multiply by 2 × 5 = 10. 40 × 10 = 400 = 2^{4} × 5^{2} = 20^{2} ✓.

questions.q: 60 = 2^{2} × 3 × 5 and 126 = 2 × 3^{2} × 7. Draw a Venn diagram of the prime factors of 60 and 126. Use it to find the HCF and the LCM of 60 and 126.
questions.ms: 1 mark: correct Venn diagram — overlap 2 and 3; 60 only: 2 and 5; 126 only: 3 and 7. 1 mark: HCF = 6. 1 mark: LCM = 1260. Allow FT for HCF and LCM from their diagram if it has one error.

blocks.title: Remember
items: A prime has exactly two factors. 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime.
Write a number as a product of primes with a factor tree or the ladder, in order, in index form: 360 = 2^{3} × 3^{2} × 5.
HCF: shared primes, smaller powers (the overlap of the Venn diagram).
LCM: all primes, larger powers (everything in the Venn diagram).
Largest equal groups/pieces → HCF. Together again / smallest common number → LCM.
Check: HCF × LCM = the product of the two numbers.
